items.stem: What authority should Claude Code automation in CI retain by default?

options.text: Advisory: it can summarise and flag, but humans approve merges and deploys
options.rationale: Correct: keeping merge and deploy authority with people preserves control.

options.text: Full authority to merge and deploy unattended
options.rationale: Unattended merge/deploy removes human oversight of risk.

options.text: No ability to read the code at all
options.rationale: That would prevent it from adding any review value.

options.text: Authority to delete branches it dislikes
options.rationale: Destructive actions must not be automated unattended.

items.explanation: Correct: keeping merge and deploy authority with people preserves control.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO make an automated PR review trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It records what it checked and what it did not
options.rationale: Correct: an audit trail bounds how much to trust the review.

options.text: Humans retain final approval on merges
options.rationale: Correct: a human gate keeps accountability with people.

options.text: It merges automatically when it finds no issues
options.rationale: Silent auto-merge removes the human oversight that review needs.

options.text: It hides its reasoning to keep the PR clean
options.rationale: Hidden reasoning cannot be audited or trusted.

items.explanation: Correct: an audit trail bounds how much to trust the review.

items.stem: A CI check fails. The best first response with Claude Code is to:

options.text: Read the job log to identify the root cause before acting
options.rationale: Correct: reading the failure log is faster and safer than blind re-runs.

options.text: Re-run the job repeatedly hoping it passes
options.rationale: Blind re-runs waste time and can mask a real failure.
Disabling checks removes the signal rather than addressing it.

options.text: Merge anyway since it is probably flaky
options.rationale: Assuming flakiness without evidence can ship a real defect.

items.explanation: Correct: reading the failure log is faster and safer than blind re-runs.
